claims.claim: Counts may be truncated to {0,1,2} without losing any information relevant to level-3 restoration.
claims.evidence: For h(r)=min(2,r), h(a+b)=min(2,h(a)+h(b)) and h(ab)=min(2,h(a)h(b)) for all nonnegative integers. The transfer recurrences use only addition and multiplication of counts, and every uniqueness test distinguishes exactly 0, 1, and at least 2. Saturation therefore preserves all information queried by both nested uniqueness quantifiers.
claims.witness: The saturated semiring homomorphism, combined with induction through both transfer layers, proves the claim. The checker also tested both identities on 16,641 integer pairs.
claims.search_method: Direct algebraic proof from the source semantics, supplemented by independent exact-integer checks; no web or unauthorized evidence used.

claims.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is decidable in O(m n^3) time under the source paper’s complexity convention.
claims.evidence: For fixed type-3 and type-2 digits, the two-coordinate q-state is exactly the saturated count of type-1 prefixes by outgoing carry. Lifting to a 9-coordinate d-state exactly counts type-2 prefixes by q-state. Filtering terminal q-states with q(alpha)=1 and requiring their saturated d-total to equal 1 implements ∃!v2:∃!v1; reachability over local type-3 choices implements ∃v3. The state spaces are constant and each three-cell column has at most n^3 combined local assignments, yielding O(m n^3) under the stated convention.
claims.witness: Independent literal evaluation agreed with the lifted recurrence on all 31,502 base-2 layouts having zero, one, or two columns, all five cell kinds, and both terminal carries.
claims.search_method: Re-derived both prefix-count invariants and the runtime, then exhaustively compared the recurrence with literal nested-quantifier semantics.

claims.claim: The same construction places every fixed-level additive restoration problem in P.
claims.evidence: A deterministic N-state recognizer for the already-eliminated lower types lifts through one global uniqueness quantifier to a deterministic recognizer with states in {0,1,2}^N. Its transition sums over local assignments, and its accepting states are precisely vectors whose saturated total over the old accepting set is 1. Induction over the inner types gives a finite tower of state counts depending only on the fixed level. The outer existential type is ordinary layered reachability. With only three cells per column, local enumeration remains polynomial under the source convention.
claims.witness: The general counting-lift invariant proves preservation of each nested exactly-one quantifier; no step depends on the number of columns or base except through local transition computation.
claims.search_method: Generalized the verified level-3 recurrence by induction on the number of inner uniqueness quantifiers and checked quantifier order and empty-type cases.

claims.claim: For every fixed level and fixed base, additive restoration is a regular language of column words under the natural encoding.
claims.evidence: With level and base fixed, the column alphabet and the iteratively lifted inner state set are finite. A column together with a local outer-type assignment determines one state transition. Allowing all such assignments gives a finite NFA whose paths correspond exactly to complete outer assignments, because restoration blanks are independent cell variables. Its accepting endpoints implement the remaining nested predicate. Reversal handles the opposite column order, and regular languages are closed under reversal.
claims.witness: The described NFA has a level- and base-dependent but length-independent finite state set; powerset determinization supplies the claimed DFA.
claims.search_method: Audited the finite-alphabet construction from first principles, including blank locality, terminal-carry handling, empty outer types, and column-order reversal.

claims.claim: Under the natural column encoding, EVEN PARITY reduces to level-3 additive restoration by a constant-block projection, already in base 2 with no type-3 cells.
claims.evidence: Direct enumeration gives A the identity carry matrix and B the saturated matrix [[2,1],[1,2]]. The two choices in C map (a,b) to (a,0) and (0,b). Recomputing the resulting d-states gives D0→D1→D2→D3→D4→D3 under T, while I is the identity. Terminal carry 0 accepts exactly D0, D2, and D4, hence exactly even Hamming weights. An empty type-3 tuple has one assignment, and fixed-length symbol coding makes every output bit a constant or an input literal.
claims.witness: The exact checker reproduced every stated D-state and verified all 511 binary words of length at most eight.
claims.search_method: Independently derived the three local transfers, multiplied the saturated states, and tested the block construction with exact arithmetic.

claims.claim: Under the natural column encoding, level-3 additive restoration is not in AC0, even when restricted to base 2.
claims.evidence: Claim 4 supplies an AC0 constant-block projection from EVEN PARITY to valid base-2 level-3 instances. Closure of AC0 under composition would put EVEN PARITY in AC0 if the restricted restoration language were in AC0, contradicting the standard parity lower bound. The same projection also targets the unrestricted language.
claims.witness: The independently verified projection preserves acceptance exactly for every tested word, and the logical reduction uses the established nonuniform AC0 parity lower bound.
claims.search_method: Checked reduction direction, validity of restricted outputs, projection locality, and the closure argument.

claims.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is formally P-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions, but this vacuous completeness convention does not provide the requested matching hardness classification.
claims.evidence: Membership follows from claim 1. The language has fixed YES and NO instances: in base 2 with terminal carry 0, x(type 3)+0=0 is satisfiable while x(type 3)+1=0 is not. For any L in P, deciding membership in L and selecting the corresponding fixed instance is a polynomial-time many-one reduction. Thus the stated completeness is formally correct but applies to every nontrivial P language and supplies no conventional structural hardness result.
claims.witness: The checker evaluated both fixed instances under literal and lifted level-3 semantics and obtained YES and NO respectively.
claims.search_method: Verified nontriviality directly and reconstructed the generic polynomial-time many-one reduction; distinguished it from logspace P-hardness.

target_evidence: The draft rigorously establishes a polynomial-time upper bound, extends it to every fixed level, proves fixed-base regularity, and gives a nonvacuous parity/AC0 lower bound. It does not provide a matching hardness classification for the polynomial-time upper bound: polynomial-time-many-one P-completeness is explicitly recognized as vacuous, and no logspace P-hardness or equivalent tight classification is proved. The draft labels itself PARTIAL, which accurately describes its coverage of the exact target.
